author: FindMeRates Desk
content:
## The numbers this week

The Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey (PMMS) puts the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate at **7.28%** for the week ending November 19, 2026, up from **7.11%** the week before — a rise of 17 basis points. The 15-year fixed rose to **6.66%**, up from **6.45%** (up 21 basis points).

A year ago, the same survey showed 6.24% for the 30-year fixed and 5.49% for the 15-year. That is 104 basis points higher than a year ago on the 30-year.

## The 12-week arc

The 30-year rate peaked at 7.40% in the weeks ending October 8 and October 15, then fell for five straight weeks to 7.11% on November 12, before this week's move back up to 7.28%. The recent low is still well above where the year started for borrowers: the survey has not printed below 7% since early September.

## What moved with it

The 10-year Treasury yield — the benchmark mortgage pricing follows most closely — was 5.04% on November 19, down from 5.15% on November 13. The weekly survey and the daily Treasury market run on different clocks, so a single week can show the two moving in opposite directions; over the last month the 10-year has mostly held between 4.84% and 5.15%.

Short-term benchmarks were steady: the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) was 3.91% on November 19, the bank prime loan rate was 7.00%, and the effective federal funds rate averaged 3.88% in October.

## What it costs on a real loan

As a worked example — not a quote — a $400,000 home loan on a 30-year fixed term costs $2,736.85 a month in principal and interest at 7.28%. At last week's 7.11% the same loan cost $2,690.83, so this week's move adds $46.02 a month. At the year-ago rate of 6.24% it would have cost $2,460.27, or $276.58 a month less. Run your own figures with our free [mortgage calculator](/calculators/mortgage) and compare [today's mortgage rates](/rates/mortgage).

## For savers

Short-term yields stayed high: the 1-year Treasury yield was 4.62% on November 19, unchanged from the day before. Savings and CD rates track these short-term benchmarks, so high-yield accounts remain well above their levels of a year ago. Compare [today's CD rates](/rates/cd) and [savings rates](/rates/savings).

## What to watch next

The next Freddie Mac survey lands Thursday, November 26 — Thanksgiving week, when survey response can be thin. The following week's survey will be the cleaner read on whether this week's rise was a pause in the fall decline or the start of a move back up. We will brief it here when it lands.

*This briefing reports published benchmark data. It is education, not a recommendation to lock, float, buy, or refinance. See our [Disclaimer](/disclaimer).*
